references.text: Abraham travels to Egypt due to a famine—the first famine mentioned, which Genesis 26:1 explicitly refers to.
Abraham goes to Gerar and stays with Abimelech, king of the Philistines—a direct parallel to Isaac's journey to the same place and under the same ruler.
The famine in Joseph's time affected the whole land, a recurring theme of famine in Genesis that also shapes the patriarchs' journeys.
The book of Ruth opens with a family leaving Bethlehem because of famine, a parallel to the patriarchs' journeys during times of famine.
Isaac repeats Abraham's mistake regarding his wife, showing a theological parallel in the testing.
A theological parallel between Isaac and Elijah who both face famine under royal rule.
